question: Will the U.S. and Argentina have signed a new 123 civil nuclear cooperation agreement as of September 10, 2026?

factors.description: Aug 10, 2026 reporting (TN, syndicated by ~10 Argentine outlets, sourced to Casa Rosada): the government's target is to sign 'antes de fin de año' and Cancillería is coordinating with Washington the steps to complete the signing 'durante los próximos meses' — plural, coming MONTHS. Nine days before question publication, the Argentine government's own framing is inconsistent with a signing in the next three weeks. Confidence discounted because ten outlets syndicating one TN piece is effectively a single source.

No US-Argentina bilateral event identified between Aug 19 and Sep 10. Every confirmed focal point falls after the deadline: UNGA Sep 22-28 (Milei + Quirno), IAEA General Conference mid-Sept, Milei in Washington Oct 14, G20 Miami Dec 14-15. Weakened because 123 signings do not require summits — Ecuador (Apr 2026) and El Salvador (Mar 2026) were signed without head-of-state visits.

No time pressure. The 1997 agreement runs to Oct 16, 2027. With a 90-day continuous-session congressional review plus Argentine ratification, the practical signing deadline is roughly Q1 2027, not 2026. Nothing forces action inside this window.

Revealed pace is slow: text reportedly closed at the Feb 25-27 JSCNEC yet still unsigned six months later. Comparator: US-Saudi took ~8 months from the Nov 2025 'Completion of Negotiations' declaration to July 2026 signature. The DOE/NNSA 123 list and CRS RS22937 still show only the 1997/2027 agreement for Argentina.

Late-August Washington is normally slow for ceremonial diplomacy (Congress in recess until ~Sep 8). Heavily discounted: the US-Paraguay NCMOU was signed by Rubio on Aug 4, 2026, squarely inside that recess, which directly undercuts this factor.

Countervailing momentum. The Trump administration has concluded regional nuclear instruments at unusual speed (El Salvador Mar 2026, Ecuador Apr 2026, Saudi Arabia Jul 2026, Paraguay NCMOU Aug 2026); US-Argentina ties are exceptionally warm (Feb 2026 reciprocal trade agreement, critical-minerals framework, FIRST membership, $1.2bn Meitner SMR at Atucha); and with the text final the residual step is a calendar slot, so a low-key State Department signing with Ambassador Oxenford needs no lead time. Hazard for a 'ripe' agreement plausibly rises rather than staying flat.

summary:
Status quo is NO and the window is only 21 days (Aug 19 to Sep 10, 00:00 UTC).

The decisive evidence is dated nine days before publication. On Aug 10, 2026, TN and ~10 syndicating Argentine outlets, sourced to Casa Rosada, reported the government aims to sign "before the end of the year," with Cancillería coordinating the diplomatic steps to complete the signature "during the coming months." That is the register of an unscheduled event. Structural corroboration: no US-Argentina bilateral engagement exists in the window, while every focal point falls after it (UNGA Sep 22-28, IAEA General Conference mid-Sept, Milei in Washington Oct 14, G20 Miami Dec 14-15). There is also no deadline pressure — the 1997 agreement runs to Oct 2027, and with a 90-day congressional review plus Argentine ratification the practical signing deadline is ~Q1 2027. Revealed pace confirms slowness: text reportedly closed at the February JSCNEC, still unsigned six months later; US-Saudi took ~8 months from completion-of-negotiations to signature. DOE/NNSA and CRS listings still show only the 1997/2027 agreement.

Rather than argue YES/NO narratively, I modelled the signing date. Two-stage: P(signed by Dec 31, 2026) ≈ 0.55 (government targets slip; the Feb-to-August gap is itself evidence of slippage) × conditional share of that mass landing in the first 21 of 134 remaining days ≈ 8-10% (uniform would be 15.7%; discounted for the later focal points) → 4.6-5.5%. A constant-hazard cross-check ignoring calendar structure gives 9.9%; a 75/25 mix gives 5.9%. Sensitivity: even assuming P(by year-end)=0.85 AND uniform timing, the ceiling is 13%.

I settle at 6%, above the 2.3% my factor stack implies because those NO factors are correlated (three framings of "nothing forces it now"), and slightly above my model's 5% because my own premortem surfaced two genuine counters from my own evidence: Paraguay's NCMOU was signed Aug 4, 2026 — inside the recess I claimed suppresses signings — and 123 agreements demonstrably get signed without summits (Ecuador, El Salvador), so a low-key State Department ceremony could land in this window with no warning. That residual possibility is why this is 6% and not 3%.
reasoning:
**Forecast submitted: 6% (NO).**

## Reasoning

**The decisive find** was Spanish-language — an English search returned only generic 123-agreement background. On **August 10, 2026**, TN (and ~10 syndicating Argentine outlets), sourced to Casa Rosada, reported the government's target is to sign *"antes de fin de año"*, with Cancillería coordinating the steps to complete the signature *"durante los próximos meses"* — plural, coming **months**. That's the register of an unscheduled event, published nine days before this question opened.

**Structural corroboration:**
- No US–Argentina bilateral engagement exists in the Aug 19 – Sep 10 window. Every focal point falls *after* it: UNGA Sep 22–28, IAEA General Conference mid-Sept, Milei in Washington Oct 14, G20 Miami Dec 14–15.
- No deadline pressure — the 1997 agreement runs to Oct 2027, so the practical signing deadline is ~Q1 2027.
- Revealed pace is slow: text reportedly closed at the February JSCNEC, still unsigned six months later. US–Saudi took ~8 months from "Completion of Negotiations" to signature.

**Modelling rather than narrative:** two-stage — P(signed by Dec 31, 2026) ≈ 0.55, times the conditional share landing in the first 21 of 134 remaining days (~8–10%, vs. 15.7% uniform) → ~5%. A constant-hazard cross-check ignoring calendar structure gives 9.9%. Even assuming P(by year-end)=0.85 *and* uniform timing, the ceiling is 13%.

**Why 6% and not 3%:** my own premortem surfaced two counters from my own evidence — Paraguay's NCMOU was signed **Aug 4, 2026**, inside the August recess I'd claimed suppresses signings, and 123 agreements demonstrably get signed without summits (Ecuador April, El Salvador March). A low-key State Department ceremony with Argentina's ambassador could land with no warning. I moved up from 5% accordingly.
